Continuing with the corrected values:

For the small primes below \(41\), we have representations:
\[
\begin{aligned}
2&=3^1-2^0,\\
3&=2^2-3^0,\\
5&=2^3-3^1,\\
7&=3^2-2^1,\\
11&=3^3-2^4,\\
13&=2^4-3^1,\\
17&=3^4-2^6,\\
19&=3^3-2^3,\\
23&=2^5-3^2,\\
29&=2^5-3^1,\\
31&=2^5-3^0,\\
37&=2^6-3^3.
\end{aligned}
\]

Now show \(41\) cannot be represented as \(|2^a-3^b|\).

If \(2^a-3^b=41\), then for \(a\ge 3\), reducing mod \(8\) gives
\[
-3^b\equiv 1 \pmod 8 \implies 3^b\equiv 7 \pmod 8,
\]
impossible since powers of \(3\) mod \(8\) are only \(1,3\). The cases \(a=0,1,2\) give no solution.

If \(3^b-2^a=41\), then for \(a\ge 3\):
\[
3^b\equiv 41\equiv 1 \pmod 8 \implies b\text{ even}.
\]
Also mod \(3\),
\[
-2^a\equiv 41\equiv 2 \pmod 3 \implies 2^a\equiv 1 \pmod 3 \implies a\text{ even}.
\]
Write \(b=2c\). Mod \(5\), since \(3^{2c}=9^c\equiv (-1)^c\pmod 5\):
- If \(c\) is even, then \(1-2^a\equiv 1\pmod 5\), so \(2^a\equiv 0\pmod 5\), impossible.
- If \(c\) is odd, then \(-1-2^a\equiv 1\pmod 5\), so \(2^a\equiv 3\pmod 5\), forcing \(a\equiv 3\pmod 4\), contradicting \(a\) even.

The cases \(a=0,1,2\) also give no solution. Thus \(41\) is not a difference of a power of \(2\) and a power of \(3\).

Therefore, the smallest prime which is not such a difference is
\[
\boxed{41}.
\]
